newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court mulling re-election injunction.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court mulling re-election injunction.

text.p: Brazil's highest court, the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF), was working on a request that voting on re-election in Congress be suspended until February and a decision might be announced later Friday, an STF spokeswoman said.

STF president Sepulveda Pertence was studying the request for an injunction that would take a constitutional amendment allowing re-election off the agenda of a special, month-long session of Congress, the spokeswoman said.
"There's a small chance that there will be a decision later today," the spokeswoman said.

On Wednesday, the Brazilian Progresive Party (PPB) filed a motion with the STF, arguing that the way the extraordinary session session had been called, first by the presidency and then again by the heads of the Senate and Chamber of Deputies, was unconstitutional.
The PPB wants the STF to rule that Congress must stick to the agenda of the first extraordinary session request, which did not include re-election.

The PPB is the party of former Sao Paulo mayor Paulo Maluf, whose own presidential ambitions depend largely on defeating the re-election amendment and sidelining President Fernando Henrique Cardoso from the 1998 presidential race.
